name: textmap
algorithm: Overwrite churn on each language's standard string-keyed hash map: per round a fresh map, n Sets of the decimal digits of splitmix64 values modulo n / 4 + 1 (three in four overwrite), then n Replaces of a second stream, each adding the old value (or 1 for a new key) to the checksum; a key is copied only when new (README.md).

skip.c: no std hash map in C
skip.mk-wrap: the checksum already uses the wrapping operators; there is no checked arithmetic to remove

no_counts: B24 does not apply: an idiomatic row compares libraries, each with its own map; the checksum (every old value, every new key, the final length) checks that every map held the same keys and values
notes: Hashes and DoS posture (B20): mk TextMap.New, DD-5's fast fixed hash, public key; mk-keyed TextMap.NewKeyed, SipHash-1-3 under a random per-process key (HashKey.New), Rust's peer, and the column Mk's ratio to Rust is quoted from; Rust HashMap, SipHash-1-3 under RandomState's random key; Zig StringHashMap, wyhash with seed 0, fixed; Go map, AES-based runtime hash seeded per map.

Key copies: Mk TextMap copies a new key into the heap and frees it at Free; Rust get_mut then insert(k.to_owned()); Zig getOrPut then dupe into the round's arena; Go m[string(b)] = v, whose runtime copies the key on insert. Mk and Rust validate each key as UTF-8 (str.From, std::str::from_utf8); Go and Zig take bytes.
